subject: Discovery: Logging & PII guardrails for inference — recap & next steps
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Li <samantha.li@datavault.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@dvsecurity.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-30T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Discovery: Logging & PII guardrails for inference — recap & next steps

Hi Samantha / Tom —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap from our side so we’re all aligned and to capture the asks we discussed: 

1) Primary pain points you described
- Uncontrolled token logs in current hosted proof-of-concept (sensitive customer PD and account IDs are being retained in text logs).
- No consistent redaction pipeline for free-form user inputs; downstream analytics and audit tools ingest raw prompts.
- Retention policy is unclear across teams (security wants 90 days TTL with auditability; compliance requires selective longer retains for legal holds).

2) Current stack (your inputs)
- Front-end: React + proxy that calls our LLM endpoints
- Inference: self-hosted open model endpoints (in-house microservices) today; considering replacing with managed inference for predictable SLAs and centralized controls
- Observability: ELK stack + custom audit db (Kafka->Postgres)

3) Success criteria you called out
- All inference requests containing PII must be redacted at the ingress or never stored verbatim in any long-term logs.
- Full audit trail for decisions: who called the model, request metadata (not raw PII), retention TTL per namespace, and immutable audit logs accessible to your SecOps.
- Ability to run forensic exports for legal holds (CSV/NDJSON) with provenance metadata.

4) Constraints / non-starters
- No raw prompt retention in S3/backups beyond 24 hours unless explicitly flagged for legal hold.
- Any managed partner must support customer-managed KMS (HSM/KMS) for key separation.

5) Proposed Redwood approach (high-level)
- Option A: Redwood Private (VPC) — customer control plane + no egress of raw prompts to Redwood-hosted logs; configurable retention and redaction at the edge.
- Option B: Redwood Dedicated with enforced prefix/KV caching & automatic redaction rules plus immutable audit log export to your ELK.
- We’ll provide an integration blueprint for Kafka/ELK sinks and a sample redaction lambda you can drop into the proxy.

Attached: redaction_guidelines_v1.pdf (sample rules), redaction_sample_config.json (example config), mmp-inference-arch.png (integration sketch).

Next steps (proposed):
- Action 1 (Technical deep-dive): Schedule a 60-min security/arch deep-dive next week with your SecOps and our infra security lead (Karthik) to review redaction patterns, audit log format, and KMS integration.
- Action 2 (POC scope): Prepare a short mutual action plan to validate: redaction on ingress, configurable retention, and audit-export to your ELK (2–3 week POC).
- Action 3 (Compliance artifacts): I’ll share a list of SOC2 / logging artifacts we can provide pre-POC.

If this aligns, I’ll send calendar invites for the deep-dive — suggested times: Tue 9/1 10:00-11:00am PT or Wed 9/2 2:00-3:00pm PT.

Thanks — appreciate the transparency on constraints, that helps us scope the right integration.

—
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0124

From: Samantha Li <samantha.li@datavault.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@dvsecurity.com>
Date: 2026-08-30T17:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery: Logging & PII guardrails for inference — recap & next steps

Jordan — thanks for the thorough recap. Quick clarifications / asks from our side: 

- Confirm raw prompts: we cannot allow raw prompt snapshots into any third-party logs beyond 24 hours. Aggregated telemetry (token counts, latency) is fine.
- Redaction: need both deterministic masking (SSN, emails) and a catch-all NLP redaction for free-form PII. Will want to validate false-negative rates in POC.
- Legal hold export: must include request_id, timestamp, caller_id (role), and model_version; raw text only permitted if legally held and encrypted under our keys.

Agreed on deep-dive — Tue 9/1 10am PT works for us. Please include a short agenda and the expected attendees (we’ll add our SecOps lead Karen Nguyen).

Also can you share the specific audit-log schema you propose and any sample immutability guarantees (append-only store + signed snapshots)? Tom, can you confirm you’ll join the deep-dive?

Thanks,
Samantha Li
Director, Platform Engineering — DataVault Systems
Samantha.li@datavault.com | +1 (650) 555-9888

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Li <samantha.li@datavault.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-31T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery: Logging & PII guardrails for inference — recap & next steps

Samantha / Jordan — happy to join Tue and to lead the security/arch deep-dive. High-level notes I’ll cover:

- Proposed audit-log schema (we’ll attach a JSON sample): request_id, timestamp (RFC3339), caller_id, model_id, model_version, tokens_in, tokens_out, event_type, retention_ttl, redaction_flag, kinesis/elk_sink_meta.
- Immutability options: append-only S3 with AWS S3 Object Lock (governance mode) or push-only Kafka topic with ACLs; we can support signed snapshots for export.
- Redaction pipeline: hybrid approach — deterministic regex rules + ML classifier with confidence thresholds + human-in-the-loop quarantine for low-confidence items. We’ll show how to tune thresholds for FN/FPR tradeoffs.
- KMS: support for customer-managed keys (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, or HSM) — keys used for encrypting any persisted raw artefacts.

I’ll come with the sample artifacts for the meeting. Jordan — can you please include the DocuSign / procurement contact on the invite so we can surface any contract redline risks early?

—Karthik
Principal Infra Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
